title: Revised Staff Reports - Federal Reserve Bank of New York

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This is a meta-index page listing Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff reports that were revised in 2016, organized by revision year. The page serves as a catalog/browse interface rather than containing substantive research content. Relevant market structure topics include: collateral use in repo markets (SR 758), dealer balance sheets and bond liquidity (SR 803), Treasury ECN microstructure (SR 381), market liquidity after the financial crisis (SR 796), and money market fund competition (SR 753).
key_points: Source is a listing_page (catalog/index), not a research document or archival record per se.
Contains approximately 40+ staff reports revised in 2016, with original releases spanning 2006-2016.

Market structure relevant papers include: SR 758 on bilateral repo and securities lending collateral, SR 803 on dealer balance sheets and bond liquidity, SR 381 on Treasury ECN BrokerTec microstructure.
Macro-related papers include: SR 804 on financial vulnerability and monetary policy, SR 690 on monetary policy and financial stability.
Page is navigation/index infrastructure rather than source material; actual research content would be in individual paper URLs.
Publication dates for individual papers range from 2006 to 2016, with revisions through 2017.
why_it_matters: This listing page is not directly archiveable as research content—it is infrastructure for discovering staff reports. However, it provides a curated index of New York Fed research on market structure topics (repo markets, dealer balance sheets, Treasury microstructure, money market funds) that may be relevant for retrieval. Users seeking specific research must navigate to individual paper pages.
market_structure_context: Several listed papers address market structure topics: SR 758 (collateral in bilateral repo/securities lending), SR 803 (dealer balance sheets and bond liquidity), SR 381 (Treasury ECN BrokerTec microstructure), SR 796 (market liquidity after financial crisis), SR 753 (money market fund competition). However, this listing page itself contains no new market structure analysis.
